solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Useful plant, one doing badly

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: doing something badly scrambles it, so the letters of doing are jumbled

explanation.surface: A plant that earns its keep, set beside one that is failing to thrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a plant grown for the blue dye extracted from its leaves, hence useful.

clue.text: Result of implosion badly ruins hotel

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are put in a poor, disordered arrangement

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A demolition by implosion goes wrong and wrecks a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: When something implodes, matter rushes inward, so an inrush is the consequence.

clue.text: Is ardent love during romantic meeting fair?

indicators.note: during means occurring within, so the other words sit inside the meeting

parts.note: a date is a romantic engagement
passion is ardent love

explanation.surface: Asks whether fervent love on a date can be fair.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites romance; the answer is its opposite, unemotional.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispassionate judgment is impartial and unbiased, hence fair.

clue.text: Italian ice creams with new food ingredient

parts.note: gelati is the Italian plural of gelato, ice cream

explanation.surface: Italian ice creams made with a novel ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatin is a setting agent used in cooking jellies and desserts.

clue.text: Reported effect of traffic jam in Paris? Sad

indicators.note: reported means the words that follow are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.words: effect of traffic jam in Paris
parts.note: a Paris street (French rue) clogged by a jam would be a rue full

explanation.surface: A gloomy comment on what a Parisian traffic jam does to a driver's mood.
explanation.walkthrough: Rue is French for street; a jammed street is a 'rue full', which said aloud is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rueful means showing regret, a mournful or sorrowful attitude.

clue.text: Headgear but not the topper in town

indicators.note: not the topper means drop the top letter, which in a down clue is the first

parts.note: a turban is a head covering

explanation.surface: Wearing a turban but no top hat around town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topper' looks like a top hat; here it is the turban's first letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban describes something belonging to a city, i.e. located in town.

clue.text: Golfer's action to succeed with first two of three below par?

parts.note: to follow is to succeed, come after
the first two letters of the word three
rough means unwell, below par; in golf the rough is also off the fairway

explanation.surface: A golfer hopes to win with two out of three holes under par.
explanation.walkthrough: TH is the first two letters of 'three'; 'below par' also hints at golf scores but here means feeling ROUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: The follow-through is the continuation of a golf swing after striking the ball.

clue.text: Tom, perhaps needs pounds for second legal representative

indicators.note: needs, with for, tells us one letter is required in place of another
for means in place of, so the pounds letter replaces the second letter

parts.note: Tom Sawyer is Mark Twain's boy hero, so Sawyer is an example surname
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A man named Tom needs money to pay a second legal adviser.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Sawyer is the title boy in Mark Twain's novel; swapping S for L gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer is a professional who represents clients in legal matters.

clue.text: Right result upset cattle thief

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the letters of result are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rancher's upset over the outcome of chasing a stock raider.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler is someone who steals livestock, especially cattle, horses or sheep.

clue.text: Eats surrounded by arguments and loud behaviour

indicators.note: surrounded by means the eating word sits inside the arguments word

parts.note: rows are noisy arguments
dines means eats

explanation.surface: A meal amid quarrels and raucous conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdiness is noisy, disorderly conduct, a boisterous state.

clue.text: Great disappointment about English not on top

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the disappointment word surrounds the English abbreviation

parts.note: a blow is a sudden setback or disappointment

explanation.surface: An English team's great disappointment at failing to reach the summit of the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Something below sits beneath another thing, so is not uppermost.

clue.text: Begin royal house when banishing first of usurpers

indicators.note: banishing means sending away, so a letter is removed from the royal name

parts.note: the Stuarts were the royal house of Scotland and later England

indicators.note: first of picks just the opening letter of usurpers

explanation.surface: A royal dynasty begins its reign once a usurper is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stuarts ruled Scotland and then Britain in the 1600s; banishing U, the first of 'usurpers', leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to commence or set something going, an exact synonym verb.

clue.text: Appealing victory by a few

parts.note: a victory is a win
some means a few, an unspecified small number

explanation.surface: A narrow win that is nonetheless pleasing to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Winsome describes charming, attractive qualities that draw people in.

clue.text: Feeling thrilled about November period

indicators.note: about means the thrilled word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: sent is informal for thrilled or carried away with delight
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a period is a stretch of time

explanation.surface: Someone feels a thrill on reflecting about a period in November.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is a view or emotional attitude, as in a feeling one holds.

clue.text: Clear up former flat

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a plain is flat land

explanation.surface: Tidying a former flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain is to clarify or make understandable.

clue.text: Coming at intervals in spring crocuses exceed daffodils at first

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of each of the three flower words

explanation.surface: In springtime crocuses outnumber daffodils early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is a SPA; CED comes from the first letters of crocuses, exceed, daffodils.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaced things are set apart with gaps, so they occur at intervals.

clue.text: Fashion to follow as an alternative

parts.note: to tail is to follow someone closely
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Following fashion as an alternative way of dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: To tailor is to make or shape clothes, hence to fashion them.

clue.text: Outline for dossier

parts.note: pro is Latin-derived for in favour of, i.e. for
a dossier is a file of documents

explanation.surface: A sketch prepared to go into someone's dossier.
explanation.definitionFit: A profile is a side-view silhouette or brief outline of a person or thing.

clue.text: I pine for perfection

parts.note: deal is timber of pine or fir

explanation.surface: Someone yearning for the perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like a verb for yearning; it is the wood DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a standard of perfection one aims for.

clue.text: Put down and leave a jacket

parts.note: to park is to set something down and leave it, as a car

explanation.surface: An instruction to take off a jacket, lay it down and walk away.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof coat, a kind of outdoor garment.

clue.text: Long for clubs with electronic dance music

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
rave is a genre of electronic dance music

explanation.surface: Pining for nightclubs that play electronic dance music.
explanation.definitionFit: To crave is to desire something intensely, a yearning.

clue.text: A fool chasing home counties bird

indicators.note: chasing means following, so the fool pieces come after the region

parts.note: SE stands for south-east, where England's home counties lie around London
to gull is to fool; a gull is also a dupe

explanation.surface: An idiot chases a bird across the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The home counties are the counties surrounding London, in the south-east (SE) of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A seagull is a common coastal bird of the gull family.

clue.text: Work persistently beside river with great intensity

indicators.note: beside means placed next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another on the England-Wales border
to ply is to work steadily at something

explanation.surface: Someone toiling hard on a riverbank, absorbed in the task.
explanation.definitionFit: Deeply means profoundly or to a great degree, as in deeply moved.

clue.text: Second piece of pollen removed from another part of stamen

indicators.note: removed from means one letter is taken out of the following word
second piece of picks the second letter of pollen

explanation.surface: A botanist notes pollen being removed from another flower's stamen.
explanation.walkthrough: The second letter of 'pollen' is O; take it out of ANOTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: The anther is the pollen-bearing tip of a flower's stamen, a botanical term.
